components.gap: Supply the complete stated component under the exact original row/notes and the declared mathematical conventions: avoid treating an abstract model's existence as a computable presentation. On the route, Theorem thm:p03-q-computably-categorical (handbook/parts/p03/finite-model-theory.tex 229-233, status proved=annex:p3.finite.1) concludes 'In particular, (Q,<) is computably categorical', a property that def:p03-computably-categorical (lines 218-220) defines only for a computable structure. The abstract structure (Q,<), whose domain is Q and not a subset of N, is thereby used as a computable structure, yet no computable presentation of (Q,<) (a presentation with domain contained in N together with a decision procedure for its coded atomic diagram, which the chapter's own rule at body lines 322-327 demands of any claim that a structure is computable) is exhibited or proved to exist anywhere on the route: annex:p3.finite.1 (handbook/annex/p03/editorial-proofs.tex 3-19) starts from two given computable copies, the uniform corollary and its annex (frontiers-of-computability.tex 622-627, annex/p04/frontiers.tex 3-23) are conditional on valid indices, and the chapter (body 352-358, 437-444) only cross-refers to the theorem. Exhibit and prove a computable presentation of (Q,<) with a decision procedure for its coded diagram (for instance from the rational coding of def:p04-rs-rational-code) and tie the 'In particular' clause to it, so that no computability claim about (Q,<) rests on the abstract model alone. The source-identification half of the component is supplied: body 35-56 names the 25 June 2019 draft of Montalban's Part 1 as the followed version, states that the version of record was not consulted, and every locator was verified in that draft (p. xviii; Def. I.1 pp. 1-2; Def. I.2 p. 2; Sect. I.1.2 pp. 2-3; Sect. I.1.3 and Obs. I.3 pp. 3-4; Sect. I.1.5 p. 4; Lemma III.15 p. 40; Def. VIII.1 p. 123; p. 124 footnote and attribution).
components.basis: Source treatment identified and accurate at every locator opened. Explicit avoidance statements present (body 5-9, 322-327, 395-398; read-only entry 209-212; P4 629-631) and a proved counterexample (no-copy theorem). But the same computable-model-theory entry applies computable categoricity to the abstract (Q,<) without any computable presentation, which is the conflation the component forbids and leaves the theorem's 'In particular' clause resting on an unproved, unexhibited dependency.

defect_observations: Body 402-404 (warning item 5): 'Changing ... the literal coding ... does not change which presentations are computable' is stated without restriction or proof; it holds only for recodings computably intertranslatable with def:p03-w03-p03-063-sentence-coding (an arbitrary injective recoding can change computability).

Annex 296-306 (no-copy) and 320-338 (omega-copies, Step 1) rest on thm:p04-tm-partial-recursive and thm:p04-kleene-normal-form (status cited=Kleene1952) and thm:universal-computation (inherited, status proof sketch). Applying closure under unbounded minimization (def:p04-partial-recursive) to 'the computable characteristic function of Q' silently uses the Turing-to-partial-recursive direction of thm:p04-tm-partial-recursive; only the converse direction is invoked by name. Cross-references are transparent; not counted against D-P4-011, whose components do not require these theorems.

Body 278-283: agreement of def:p03-computably-categorical with Definition VIII.1 is argued via composites and inverses of computable isomorphisms between omega-presentations (Lemma 262-276), while the chapter's 'copy' (139-151) ranges over (subset-omega)-presentations; the transfer through Theorem 288-304(a) is not stated.
